extracted.intended_audience: parties and counsel in AIA proceedings, PTAB practitioners, USPTO/PTAB staff, patent attorneys/agents
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory procedures and substantive availability rules governing requests for, initiation of, processing of, and effects of Director Review of PTAB (AIA) decisions under 37 CFR part 42. Targets how parties request review, what decisions are reviewable, timeline/format/content limits, delegation, communications, and appealability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director Review — availability (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a proceeding under this part, the Director may review any decision on institution under 35 U.S.C. 135, 314, or 324, any final decision under 35 U.S.C. 135, 318, or 328, any decision granting rehearing of such a decision, or any other decision concluding a proceeding brought under 35 U.S.C. 135, 311, or 321.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For purposes of this section, the term 'final decision' is defined as a 'final decision' under 35 U.S.C. 135 as well as a 'final written decision' under 35 U.S.C. 318 or 328. The Director may also review any interlocutory decision rendered by the Board in reaching that decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sua sponte Director Review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director, on the Director’s own initiative, may initiate sua sponte Director Review of a decision as provided in paragraph (a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absent exceptional circumstances, any sua sponte Director Review will be initiated within 21 days after the expiration of the period for filing a request for rehearing pursuant to § 42.71(d). The rule leaves the Director flexibility to initiate sua sponte review and does not restrict the Director by rule to particular categories of issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Party request — one request in lieu of rehearing
rubrics_metrics.description: A party to a proceeding may file one request for Director Review of an eligible decision instead of filing a request for rehearing of that decision pursuant to § 42.71(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties are limited to requesting either Director Review or rehearing by the original panel, but may not request both; requests for both are treated as a request for Director Review only. A party may file only one request for Director Review of a given decision, subject to limitations and any further guidance provided by the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for filing requests
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for Director Review must be filed within the time period set forth in § 42.71(d) unless an extension is granted by the Director upon a showing of good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No response to a Director Review request is permitted absent Director authorization. The rule permits extensions upon a showing of good cause, and the burden is on the requesting party to establish entitlement to the extension (consistent with 37 CFR 42.20(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and length of requests
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for Director Review must comply with the format requirements of § 42.6(a) and, absent Director authorization, must comply with the length limitations for motions to the Board provided in § 42.24(a)(1)(v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may authorize deviations from format/length. Parties must file requests in the Patent Trial and Appeal Case Tracking System and send an email to Director_PTABDecision_Review@uspto.gov as described on the Director Review web page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content limitations — no new evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Absent Director authorization, a request for Director Review may not introduce new evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests should rely on the existing record; where new evidence is proposed, Director authorization is required before it may be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality of Board decisions subject to Director Review
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision on institution, a final decision, a decision granting rehearing of such decision, or any other decision concluding a proceeding shall become the final agency decision unless a party requests rehearing or Director Review within the time provided by § 42.71(d) (or an extension is granted) or the Director initiates sua sponte review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon denial of a request for Director Review of a final decision (or of a decision granting rehearing of a final decision), the Board’s decision becomes the final agency decision. The underlying Board decision does not become final if there is an extension of time for a party to file a request for Director Review (to conform paragraph (d) with paragraph (c)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on underlying proceeding (stays/non-stays)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless the Director orders otherwise, and except as provided in paragraph (e)(3), a request for Director Review or initiation of sua sponte review does not stay the time for the parties to take action in the underlying proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director has discretion to order otherwise. The rule does not automatically suspend deadlines in the underlying PTAB proceeding upon a Director Review request.

rubrics_metrics.name: If Director grants review — record and disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director grants Director Review, the Director shall issue an order or decision that will be made part of the public record, subject to protective orders or other confidentiality requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Director grants review and does not subsequently withdraw the grant, the Director Review will conclude with the issuance of a decision or order that provides the reasons for the Director’s disposition of the case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appealability of Director Review decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may appeal a Director Review decision of a final decision under 35 U.S.C. 135, 318, or 328, a decision granting rehearing of a final decision under those statutes, or any other appealable decision concluding a proceeding brought under 35 U.S.C. 135, 311, or 321, to the United States Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit using the same procedures for appealing other decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director Review decisions on decisions on institution are not appealable. A request for Director Review (or initiation of sua sponte review) of an appealable decision will be treated as a request for rehearing under § 90.3(b)(1) of this chapter and will reset the time for appeal until after all issues on Director Review in the proceeding are resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of Director Review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may delegate their review of a decision provided in paragraph (a) of this section, subject to any conditions provided by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule allows the Director to delegate review at the Director’s discretion and to identify the delegated decision-maker(s). The Office will provide additional guidance on delegation on the Director Review web page; delegation is permitted but not mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte communications and third-party participation
rubrics_metrics.description: All communications from a party to the Office concerning a specific Director Review request or proceeding must copy counsel for all parties. Communications from third parties regarding a specific Director Review request or proceeding, aside from authorized amicus briefing, are not permitted and will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third parties may not request Director Review or communicate with the USPTO concerning the Director Review of a particular case unless the Director invites them to do so. The Director retains authority to request or permit amicus briefing where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Committee review and recommendation process
rubrics_metrics.description: Each request for Director Review is considered by an Advisory Committee that assists the Director and presents a recommendation (consensus or noting differing views).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Advisory Committee has at least 11 members from multiple USPTO business units (Office of the Under Secretary excluding Director/Deputy Director; PTAB excluding original panel members; Office of the Commissioner for Patents excluding Commissioner or examiners of challenged patent; Office of the General Counsel including Solicitor; Office of Policy and International Affairs). Meetings may proceed with a quorum of seven members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on introducing new procedural requirements by rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule does not adopt prescriptive standards of review (e.g., de novo, clear error, abuse of discretion) or rigid time limits for completion of Director Review; the Director retains flexibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office declined commenters’ suggestions to codify standards of review, strict deadlines (e.g., 30 days to decide whether to grant/deny or 3 months to complete review), or mandatory delegation; instead, guidance will be provided on the Director Review web page and the Director retains discretion to apply appropriate standards and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of reviewable proceedings (inclusions/exclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule expressly provides Director Review for derivation proceedings under 35 U.S.C. 135 and for any other decision concluding an AIA proceeding brought under 35 U.S.C. 135, 311, or 321; the rule does not expand Director Review to ex parte appeals, reexamination, or reissue appeals at this time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of 'other decision concluding a proceeding' include termination due to a grant of adverse judgment or dismissal of a proceeding. The Office considered but did not adopt expanding Director Review to appeals from ex parte examination and reexaminations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing mechanics and public status
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director grants review, the Director shall issue an order or decision that will be made part of the public record, subject to protective orders or confidentiality rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must be filed in the PTAB Case Tracking System and an email sent to the Director at Director_PTABDecision_Review@uspto.gov. Status of Director Review requests is published on the Director Review status web page (spreadsheet updated monthly).
